title: Power-Seeking Behavior as a Measurable Activation Pattern: A Replication and Extension Study

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: a generalizable, causally-verified power-seeking feature would be among the most safety-relevant interpretability findings. Even a null result calibrates where to focus detection efforts for agentic misalignment.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Designing diverse power-seeking scenarios (resource acquisition, oversight avoidance, self-preservation), probing for generalized features across scenario types, and performing causal steering is advanced for beginner CS students with 30 hours.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Sustained effort: scenario design across multiple power-seeking types, residual stream probing, cross-context generalization testing, and causal steering verification. The breadth of scenario types makes this scope-heavy.

novelty.reasoning: Recent work has directly addressed power-seeking detection via activation patterns. 'Probing Power-Seeking in LLMs' (Alignment Forum / LessWrong, 2025) investigated probing for power-seeking behavior in activation space. The SPAR project 'Pre-Emptive Detection of Agentic Misalignment via Representation Engineering' builds neural circuit breakers for detecting deception and power-seeking signatures. 'AgentMisalignment' (arXiv:2506.04018, 2025) provides benchmarks for measuring power-seeking in agents. Research found that covert power-seeking can be captured in activation-space directions from just two fine-tuned layers. The core question of whether power-seeking has a measurable activation pattern is being actively investigated, though cross-context generalization and causal steering verification remain open.
